answer: Biometric deduplication resists sybils: enrollment hashes a person's biometric template into a code on-device, and the registry rejects any new identity whose code matches an existing one, so one body yields one identity. A farmer wanting ten thousand agents must recruit ten thousand people, and a sable disguise fails because the template, not the look, is checked. Like a lotus rooting once in a pond, each person holds one slot, and no willow sway hides a duplicate. The limit is privacy and error: templates must stay on-device, and false matches can lock out users, so appeals must exist.
